analysis.summary: Missing enableConsents query parameter propagation in POST consents utility causes BFF to always use Mulesoft path

bugs.title: postConsents missing enableConsents query parameter
bugs.description: The postConsents function does not accept or propagate the enableConsents parameter as a query parameter, unlike fetchConsents which correctly adds it to the URL. The BFF handler routes requests based on the enableConsents query parameter (not the body), so POST requests always fall through to the Mulesoft path regardless of the feature flag value.
bugs.risk: Causes a functional split where GET requests respect the feature flag (CDC vs Mulesoft) but POST requests always use the Mulesoft backend, leading to inconsistent data handling and potential data corruption or loss when the CDC path is expected.

notBugs.topic: Different consent fields between CDC and Mulesoft paths
notBugs.reason: The convertCdcConsents and convertToConsents functions return different field sets (e.g., consentVocEmail vs newsletter). This is intentional as the two backends (CDC vs Mulesoft) support different consent types during the migration period. Each path is internally consistent with its own data contract.

notBugs.topic: enableConsents string truthiness in query params
notBugs.reason: While the BFF checks if (enableConsents) where enableConsents is a string, the frontend currently only sends the string 'true' or omits the parameter entirely (never sends 'false'), so the truthiness check works correctly for the current implementation.

The useConsents hook does not include enableConsents in the useEffect dependency array. Feature flags are typically constant for the session and do not change dynamically without a page reload, so this is not a runtime risk.
